## Context / Problem
No document tells a client project how to run plan-replay, fixture-mining or provider-parity against its own `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` and `.rebar/evals/`. `docs/llm-framework.md`'s "Extras taxonomy" (`:43`) still opens "The optional surface is three extras" (`:45`) — a count that was already stale and is now wrong by two: sibling story `d279` (`disgusted-fretful-hare`, closed) registered `evals` in `rebar._optional.EXTRAS`.

Separately, 71 open, parentless `fixture-drift:` tasks (e.g. `00b4-b253-3052-4181`) were filed by hand for story 67aa from `evals/plan-review-gate/fixtures/drift-report.md`, each `discovered_from` the closed epic `65dd-e93b-666a-4caa`. `git grep fixture-drift` is empty; `fixture_mining/heal.py`'s only ticket producer is `_file_unreliable_ticket` (`UNRELIABLE_TITLE_PREFIX` at `heal.py:32`, consumed at `:273`), and drift is written to `.rebar/fixture_heal_drift.md` (`heal.py:426`). Those 71 tasks have no producer and no consumer. Cites verified on `aa37a738570` plus the corpus move.

**Scope correction — the extras REGISTRATION is already done.** `d279` added the `evals` key to `EXTRAS`, routed `genai_prices` through `guard_import`, and added the `evals:evals` spec to `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml`. This story's remaining work on that axis is DOCUMENTING the extra, not registering it; the title's "register the evals extra" is satisfied upstream and no AC here re-asserts it.

## Approach
Add a `docs/llm-framework.md` section "Running the eval harnesses against your own criteria" after "Usage log" (`:471`), covering: install with `pip install 'nava-rebar[agents,evals]'`; criteria in `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` and project prompts in `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md` (override-wins ordering, `fixture_selection.rubric_path` `:38`, override branch `:52-54`); specs in `.rebar/evals/<prompt_id>.eval.yaml` beating packaged ones (`eval.py:57-78`); `[llm.evals] corpus_root` (default `.rebar/evals`, env `REBAR_LLM_EVALS_CORPUS_ROOT`).

Then the commands: `rebar prompt eval <prompt_id>`; `rebar criteria eval [<criterion_id>] --changed-since origin/main --require-live`; `rebar criteria heal --dry-run` then `rebar criteria heal` (`cap_usd=25.0`, passed to `production_attempter` at `_llm_eval_commands.py:136`; writes `.rebar/fixture_heal_drift.md`, `.rebar/fixture_heal_ledger.jsonl`, emits `.rebar/evals/*.eval.yaml`, files `unreliable-criterion: <id>` tickets); `python -m rebar.llm.evals.plan_replay tier0 --candidate current`, `tier1 --n 20`, `tier2 --criteria E1` (writing under `<corpus_root>/plan-review-gate/replay/`, `--store name=path` for another store, `--ledger` to relocate spend); `python -m rebar.llm.evals.provider_parity --slot standard --epochs 3 --out <path>`.

**`--out` has no default and is not corpus-root-relative.** `provider_parity.py:604` declares `default=None` and the write at `:649-651` is guarded by `if args.out:`, so a run without it writes nothing. `d279` deliberately left that flag unchanged, so the doc must show `--out` explicitly rather than implying an automatic location — and the release note must not claim otherwise.

Update the taxonomy's opening count at `:45` and add an `evals` bullet; add the `llm.evals.corpus_root` row to "Configuration" (`:395`); add a `[llm.evals]` snippet to `docs/llm-example-configs.md`.

**The 71 tasks are ALREADY closed — this story VERIFIES, it does not dispose.** They were bulk-closed on 2026-09-08 with `close_class: obsolete` and the reason "fixture-drift ticket mooted by ADR 0113 self-heal loop", recorded in this ticket's own comment. A `search(status:open)` transition loop would therefore match nothing and transition nothing. Replace it with a verification step, and note two traps in how it is written:
(a) `rebar search "fixture-drift:"` returns **72** rows, not 71 — the 72nd is THIS STORY, whose title contains the phrase. The 71 are `ticket_type: task`; the story is `story`, so the check must filter by type or it can never pass (the completion verifier runs BEFORE the close commits, so the story is still `open` at that moment).
(b) `rebar search -o json` does **not** project `close_class`, so a jq assertion over search output tests a field that is absent. The per-ticket property has to come from `rebar show <id> -o json`.

Release note (non-breaking, contract section): eval harness roots are configurable (`llm.evals.corpus_root`, default `.rebar/evals`); `plan_replay.ledger.DEFAULT_LEDGER_PATH` removed with ledger defaults resolving at call time, and the `evals` extra registered — BOTH landed in `d279`, like the extras registration above; this story only documents them, consistent with Scope's "no source files". No claim about `--out`.

**The doc test is generated from one source, not a hand-kept list.** Sibling story `bafa` needed six plan-review rounds because hand-enumerated references kept drifting. So `tests/unit/test_llm_framework_docs.py` derives its expectations from the data: the extras assertion iterates `rebar._optional.EXTRAS` (so a future extra fails the doc, not the test), and the command assertions read the fenced command block out of the section and compare against a module-level tuple that the test itself also uses to shell out with `--help`, so a renamed flag fails rather than silently passing.

## Scope
`docs/llm-framework.md`, `docs/llm-example-configs.md`, `docs/release-notes.md`, `tests/unit/test_llm_framework_docs.py` (new); tracker writes on the 71 tickets plus one comment. No source files, and nothing under `evals/`.

## Testing
`pytest tests/unit/test_llm_framework_docs.py -q`; `python scripts/check_docs_index.py`; each documented command run once in a temp client repo (`rebar init`, copy `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`), using `--dry-run` where offered. Edge: `rebar prompt eval nonexistent-id` names the missing spec path rather than raising a traceback; re-running the disposition batch is a no-op, each ticket already closed, so exit 10 is expected and skipped.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `docs/llm-framework.md` contains the section heading, and every command in its fenced block resolves — each one's `--help` exits 0, asserted by `test_llm_framework_docs.py`.
- [x] Every key in `rebar._optional.EXTRAS` appears in the extras taxonomy, asserted by iterating `EXTRAS` rather than against a literal count, and the taxonomy's opening sentence no longer says "three extras".
- [x] `llm.evals.corpus_root` is documented with its default `.rebar/evals` and its env name `REBAR_LLM_EVALS_CORPUS_ROOT`.
- [x] The documented `provider_parity` invocation passes `--out` explicitly, and neither the doc nor the release note claims a default output location.
- [x] Every `fixture-drift:` TASK is closed: `rebar search "fixture-drift:" -o json | jq '[.[]|select(.ticket_type=="task" and .status!="closed")]|length'` prints `0`. The type filter is required — this story's own title matches the phrase, and it is still `open` while the completion verifier runs.
- [x] Each of those tasks carries the disposition, read per ticket because `search` does not project it: `for id in $(rebar search "fixture-drift:" -o json | jq -r '.[]|select(.ticket_type=="task")|.ticket_id'); do rebar show "$id" -o json | jq -e '.close_class=="obsolete" and (.close_reason|length>0)' >/dev/null || echo "BAD $id"; done` prints nothing.
- [x] `make verify` exits 0.
